Subject: Performance MAP & close timeline - Fast Retail

Alex —

Thanks for the demo today. As discussed, we want to include a concrete Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that contains the evaluation plan and an agreed close timeline. High level asks from our side:

- A benchmarking plan that measures latency (p50/p95), TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and behavior under target concurrency (4, 8, 16).
- A short-list of model variants from your catalog with measured quality/perf tradeoffs for our primary use case (short catalog lookup + single-turn generation, typical output length ~50 tokens).
- A clear set of owners and deadlines so our procurement can move to contract signature by end of month (ideally Jun 26).

Constraints:
- Priority region: us-east; expected concurrently active sessions ~8 during peak.
- Latency target: p95 < 400ms for 50-token responses; TTFT < 150ms.
- Quality baseline: retrieval+generation accuracy >= 92% on our eval set; hallucination rate <2%.

Can you send a proposed MAP with the evaluation plan, test harness details, and initial benchmark results if available? We can provide an eval set (we'll share via Drive) and a small synthetic load script.

Thanks,
Jamie
Director of ML Platforms
Fast Retail

---

Jamie —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a first-draft MAP and evaluation plan (FR_eval_plan_v1.pdf). Summary below; the attached PDF has the full test matrix and raw-run artifacts.

Proposed MAP highlights (owners / deadlines):
- Deliverable: Controlled benchmark runs + quality eval on your eval set (owner: neha_kapoor) — target Jun 10
- Deliverable: Variant comparison report (latency/TTFT/throughput + quality) (owner: alex_martinez) — target Jun 14
- Deliverable: Final MAP & procurement-ready SOW (owner: laura_bennett) — target Jun 20
- Demo & review call (joint) — scheduled Jun 22
- Target contract signature — Jun 26

Evaluation approach (short):
- Workloads: 3 templates drawn from your sample queries — short lookup, brief summary, promo generation (mean output 45–60 tokens).
- Models to test: redwood-7b-ptq, redwood-13b-ptq, redwood-13b-fp16, open-mistral-7b-v2 (catalog names in attached plan).
- Measurement specs: measure cold start vs warmed-up, measure TTFT (wall-clock to first token), p50/p95 latency for full response, tokens/sec for sustained generation under fixed concurrency. Each cell = median of 5 runs + standard deviation.
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16 concurrent sessions; test both single-request bursts and sustained 5-minute steady-state runs.
- Quality eval: run model outputs against your labelled set (precision/recall for extraction, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and a small hallucination checklist).

Initial micro-benchmarks (informal, from our dev lab; full runs attached):
- redwood-7b-ptq (single request, warmed): TTFT 85ms, p50 160ms, p95 370ms, throughput 420 tokens/sec at concurrency=4
- redwood-13b-ptq (warmed): TTFT 110ms, p50 210ms, p95 480ms, throughput 520 tokens/sec at concurrency=4
- redwood-13b-fp16 (warmed, high perf profile): TTFT 95ms, p50 180ms, p95 420ms, throughput 600 tokens/sec at concurrency=4

First impressions: 7b-ptq is latency-friendly and meets p95 target in many short-request cases, but quality on the retail extraction subset is ~3 points lower than 13b variants. 13b-fp16 gives a good performance/quality balance but has slightly higher p95. We'll run your real eval set to quantify tradeoffs and provide recommended default (latency-first) and fallback (quality-first) variants.

Next actions: Neha will coordinate secure upload of your eval set; please confirm which IP ranges we should test from and any additional QoS constraints.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
